description: alignment.jsonl written by --alignment-out: one header line, then one line per position of the run

notes.why_one_artifact: The byte span and the probe score are one artifact keyed by run_id rather than two files joined afterwards. A probe trace over tens of thousands of positions is uninterpretable without the text each position produced, and a comparison whose join is fiddly is a comparison that does not get run often enough to be useful.
notes.positions_are_dense: Every position of the run has exactly one row, including positions consumed by chat-template scaffolding. Those are marked role=scaffold rather than omitted: omitting one renumbers every position after it, and the artifact's value rests on its indices being the run's own absolute cache positions - the same numbering the tap reports and the pass record uses.
notes.byte_spans: Spans are byte offsets into the header's 'text', half-open, and concatenating every row's span in position order reproduces that text exactly. Bytes, not characters, because the tokenizer is byte-oriented and byte-fallback pieces exist. A codepoint spread across several byte-fallback tokens is attributed whole to the position that completes it; the positions it spans carry empty spans, since no smaller attribution exists.
notes.scaffold_and_visible_text: role=scaffold does not imply an empty span. It holds for a checkpoint whose chat markers are pieces the tokenizer's decoder drops, as the real Gemma 4 vocabulary's are; the synthetic fixtures deliberately carry boundaries as ordinary vocabulary entries, so a marker there decodes to its own characters and lands in the text. The writer reports what was decoded and marks the role rather than suppressing bytes, because a suppressed byte breaks the round trip above.
notes.pass_and_phase: 'pass' is the ordinal of the forward call that computed the position, minted in CpuModel::prefill_groups, the one place a batch boundary is decided. It is recorded because the prefill/decode split alone stopped being sufficient once batching landed: it cannot distinguish a position computed alongside its neighbours from one computed alone. 'phase' is derived from that pass's width - decode reaches the backend as a prefill of a single token and there is no second entry point to observe.
notes.absent_not_null: 'pass', 'phase' and 'score' are omitted rather than written null when unavailable. A null pass would claim the position was computed by no forward call and a null score would claim the probe looked and found nothing; both are different facts from an unrecorded field. 'score' is present only for positions of the probe's own layer, and only when a probe was loaded.
notes.token_id: The id the run computed at the position. Recorded so a reader holding only the artifact and the checkpoint's tokenizer can check each span against the vocabulary, which the harness's own decode cannot vouch for: the round trip above proves the spans partition the text, not that a span holds its own token's bytes. Optional so schema_version stays 1; every row the current writer emits carries it.
notes.python_reader: tests/hardware/test_alignment.py is the one Python reader, and it is a checker rather than the longitudinal reader: on the workstation it decodes each row's token_id with transformers and holds the span to those bytes. The analysis reader this artifact exists for is still unwritten.
notes.run_id: R-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxxxx, minted by obs::mint_run_id and pinned by schemas/obs_record.json. No second identifier is invented: the same id names this run's event log, so the two artifacts join. 'unknown' when the obs log could not be opened.
notes.envelope: The header carries the shared report envelope from common/reports.py: schema_version, exactly one discriminator (artifact), a stamp (created), and git_sha.
